Subject: MAP: Performance validation & acceptance timeline (latency, TTFT, concurrency)

Hi Jenna —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Per our MAP, I want to lock down the performance validation plan so we can align the acceptance criteria and close timing with your procurement team. High-level ask: can you confirm the two workload profiles Acme will run (conversational search and batch re-ranking) and whether you need an on-prem run or hosted API evaluation?

Proposed scoping for the validation window (attached):
- Workload definitions: representative request distributions for each profile (attached CSV).
- SLOs / success criteria: p95 latency <= 350ms for short-turn chat (<=512 tokens); TTFT <= 750ms median for first-stream token on streaming endpoints; sustained concurrency target = 600 concurrent users (approx. 2,400 RPS burst profile).
- Throughput targets: 3x sustained requests/sec per GPU based on our reference model; we will provide observed QPS during runs.
- Acceptance: pass all SLOs on two consecutive soak windows (30m each) + no functional regressions in 100 synthetic prompt sample set.
- Timeline: propose validation runs Apr 7–8, analysis Apr 9, decision/close Apr 12.

Attachments: acme_map_bench_plan_v1.pdf, workload_profiles.csv

Next steps: please reply with (1) confirmation of workload profiles, (2) any additional success criteria your side requires, and (3) procurement constraints (hard close dates).

Thanks,
Hannah

Hi all —

Quick technical notes and proposed test plan details from infra: 
- Test harness: we will use a controlled loader with traffic shaping to reproduce Acme's request distribution (see workload_profiles.csv). We will run three phases per profile: warm-up (10m), ramp (20m), soak (30m).
- Metrics we will capture: token-level latency (p50/p90/p95/p99), TTFT (median + p90), sustained QPS per GPU, GPU utilization, mem footprint, KV cache hit rates.
- Failure rules: any single run where p95 exceeds target by >15% or p99 exceeds by >10% fails; functional regressions fail the validation irrespective of infra metrics.
- Concurrency mapping: 600 concurrent users maps to ~2,400 RPS for short inference with 0.25s per call average on reference model — we will calibrate with a 5-minute pilot on Apr 7 09:00 PT.

I attached a small sample results file from a comparable pilot (sample_results_q1.json) — use it as a baseline; we expect top-line numbers to be within 10–20% based on Acme's current model size.

Let us know if you want us to add additional telemetry (tracing ids, token-level breakdown exported to S3).

-karthik
